title: Structural reorganization of elite men’s water polo: A quasi-experimental multivariate analysis of the 2025 rule changes
content:
by Seung-Hun Lee

The 2025 World Aquatics rule revisions for water polo aimed to accelerate offensive tempo and alter tactical decision-making by reducing the field length, shot clock duration, and possession reset times. This study used the 2024 and 2025 Men’s Water Polo World Championships as consecutive editions of the same elite international competition to provide an initial quasi-experimental assessment of performance changes associated with these revisions. Performance indicators across four domains (offensive performance, goalkeeping, exclusions, and game management) were analyzed using a multivariate analysis of variance. Notably, significant multivariate differences were observed between tournaments across all performance domains. Subsequent univariate analyses showed that these differences were primarily reflected in the frequency and distribution of match events. Most shooting and save rates showed no statistically significant difference between tournaments. These findings suggest that performance changes associated with the 2025 rule revisions were not reflected in isolated improvements in technical efficiency but rather in a structural reorganization of match performance. Compared with 2024, teams in 2025 recorded more possessions, action shot attempts, and field exclusions per match, and fewer counterattack shot attempts. Overall, this study highlights the importance of evaluating rule-change effects at the structural level of match performance and supports the usefulness of multivariate approaches for capturing initial performance adaptations in elite water polo.
